# Introduction

Everything in epiworldR runs in C++, in the
[epiworld](https://github.com/UofUEpiBio/epiworld) library. When R functions
are not enough (an intervention that runs every day, a rate that depends on
each agent), you can write that part in C++ and add it to a model built in R.
It then runs at the speed of the rest of the model.

The C++ reaches a model with one function, `epiworldR::as_model()`, which
returns the `epiworld::Model` behind an R model. From there, the whole epiworld
C++ API is available: global events, tools, viruses with their natural
histories, layers, parameters... What the code adds belongs to the model, as if
added from R.

There are two ways to compile it:

- **In a session**, with `cpp_source_epiworld()` (this vignette).
- **In a package**: add `LinkingTo: cpp11, epiworldR` to `DESCRIPTION`,
  `CXX_STD = CXX17` to `src/Makevars`, and `#include <epiworldR/extension.h>`
  to the C++ files. The functions marked `[[cpp11::register]]` become the
  package's R functions.

The C++ must be built against the same major version of epiworld as the
installed epiworldR: `as_model()` checks this, and stops with an error saying
so if they differ. Compiling it again after updating epiworldR is safest.

# Two extensions

The code below defines two functions:

1. `add_campaign()`: a global event, run at the end of every day, that gives
   the model's vaccine to a share of the susceptible agents without it.
2. `add_waning_sirs()`: an SIRS disease whose immunity starts to wane only a
   month after recovery, a rate that reads how long each agent has been
   recovered.

```{r}
#| label: compile
library(epiworldR)

cpp_source_epiworld(code = '
// A daily vaccination campaign
class Campaign : public epiworld::GlobalEvent {
  double p_;
public:
  explicit Campaign(double p) : p_(p) { set_name("Campaign"); }

  void operator()(epiworld::Model * m, int) override {
    auto & vaccine = m->get_tool("Vaccine");
    for (auto & agent : m->get_agents())
      if ((m->get_stage(agent) == 0) && (agent.get_n_tools() == 0u) &&
          (m->runif() < p_))
        agent.add_tool(*m, vaccine);
  }

  std::unique_ptr< epiworld::GlobalEvent > clone_ptr() const override {
    return std::make_unique< Campaign >(*this);
  }
};

[[cpp11::register]]
void add_campaign(SEXP model, double p) {
  Campaign campaign(p);
  epiworldR::as_model(model).add_globalevent(campaign);
}

// SIRS, with immunity that wanes only after 30 days
[[cpp11::register]]
void add_waning_sirs(SEXP model, double prevalence) {
  epiworld::Virus flu("Flu");
  flu.add_stage("Susceptible");
  flu.add_stage("Infected", epiworld::stage::infectious);
  flu.add_stage("Recovered");
  flu.infection(0, 1, "Transmission rate");
  flu.rate(1, 2, "Recovery rate").effect(epiworld::Effect::recovery);
  flu.rate(2, 0, epiworld::ValueFun(
    [](epiworld::Agent & agent, epiworld::Model & m) -> epiworld_double {
      const int recovered = m.get_stage_entered(agent.get_id(), 2);
      return (m.today() - recovered > 30) ? 0.05 : 0.0;
    }
  ));
  epiworldR::as_model(model).add_virus(flu, epiworld::assign::share(prevalence));
}
')
```

`cpp_source_epiworld()` adds `#include <epiworldR/extension.h>`, which sets up
the epiworld headers as epiworldR uses them.

## A global event

The campaign needs a tool named `"Vaccine"` in the model, added from R and
given to no one at the start:

```{r}
#| label: campaign
model <- ModelSIR(
  "flu",
  n                 = 5000,
  prevalence        = .01,
  transmission_prob = .3,
  recovery_rate     = .1
)
add_layer(model, layer_network("contacts", graph_smallworld(10, .1)))
add_tool(model, tool("Vaccine", .9, 0, 0, 0), assign_count(0))
add_campaign(model, 0.05)
verbose_off(model)
run(model, ndays = 60, seed = 1)
plot(model)
```

## A disease with a rate written in C++

The model starts empty: it gets its parameters and its layer in R, and its
disease from C++. The transitions read the parameters by name.

```{r}
#| label: waning
model <- Model(5000)
add_param(model, "Transmission rate", 0.15)
add_param(model, "Recovery rate", 1 / 7)
add_layer(model, layer_network("contacts", graph_smallworld(10, .1)))
add_waning_sirs(model, 0.01)
verbose_off(model)
run(model, ndays = 300, seed = 1)
plot(model)
```

The infections come in waves: an agent becomes susceptible again only after
its first month as recovered.

# Going further

- The functions an extension can call are epiworld's C++ API: see the
  [epiworld documentation](https://uofuepibio.github.io/epiworld/) and its
  headers, installed with epiworldR (`system.file("include", package =
  "epiworldR")`).
- `?cpp_source_epiworld` has the details of the session route and of a
  package that links to epiworldR.
